claim_reviews.rationale: The authors report 14 morphologically assigned grains across four deposits; a cork-tree seed from one millet-bearing unit yielded BA07888, 8885±55 BP, 8240–7820 BCE at 95.4%. Grain displacement and indirect dating remain explicit.

unknowns: No direct date on the millet grains; author overlap with earlier study does not make different specimens independent excavation contexts.

records.rationale: Candidate question concerns a possible local integrated crop and pig feeding arrangement, not a developmental descent or an established connection.

claim_reviews.rationale: Rice cultivation is inferred from wetland sediment and excavated rice. Rice phytoliths in three Kuahuqiao pig specimens and cooked starch in suid calculus support exposure to rice and prepared foods, but neither the source of the rice nor deliberate feeding is demonstrated. The question and alternatives preserve those limits.

relation.vocabulary: The two worked together as parts of one arrangement.
relation.endpoint_kinds: Both are practices; the pig record has capability grain and the rice record has no explicit grain.
relation.context: The question explicitly asks if people fed managed pigs rice or rice-processing remains from local wetland cultivation at Kuahuqiao, an integrated feeding arrangement; the receiving record also includes Jingtoushan, which is excluded by scope.
relation.status: candidate: possible arrangement, not an established relation; dating overlaps but individual pig phases are unknown
relation.corroboration: Independent sediment, rachilla, and dental samples support components but do not establish deliberate feeding of cultivated rice.
relation.alternatives: Wild rice foraging, scavenging, other feeds and uncertain management.

unknowns: Exact specimen phases and route from crop to pig diet remain unknown.

records.rationale: The added question preserves a distinction between harvesting technology and inferred domestication traits.

claim_reviews.rationale: SS-10 striations and rice glume residue support interpreted panicle harvesting; independent material records Shangshan rachilla morphologies and bulliform measurements. Seed retention and contribution to particular silica traits are not demonstrated.

unknowns: Harvesting does not itself establish resowing, selection or causal contribution.

records.rationale: The same radiocarbon specimen has traceable original context; it is not independent corroboration of seed size.

claim_reviews.rationale: Huang and Li contrast pit S13 with S′ and S15 using pollen, phytolith and excavation evidence; Fuller and Qin supply the Late Majiabang 4300–4000 BCE context. The studies refer to related excavation features, not two independent excavations.
Huang and Li explicitly interpret pondweed decline as falling water and propose water scarcity prompted the change in field type; it is an attributed explanation, not direct proof.

Zheng et al. 2009 describes Tianluoshan early fields 5000–4500 BCE and reports no irrigation in early and later phases; no transmission to Lake Tai is shown. Other unresolved notes retain hydrology and chronological questions.
sources: Zheng et al. 2009, Rice fields and modes of rice cultivation, Table 1, pp. 2611–2615

unknowns: Matching Huang phase labels to the Late Majiabang record needs further stratigraphic work; modern study does not independently replicate original pit excavation.

additional_records.rationale: New local wetland cultivation evidence is a distinct site and context from later Lake Tai engineered fields and from Shangshan rice morphology.

claim_reviews.rationale: Zong describes a Kuahuqiao coastal wetland and associated rice and wild-food remains; Zheng examines rice morphology. Burning taxa are disputed by Shu and barrier construction remains a proposal.

Zong dates cultural sediments in this specific sequence about 7700–7550 cal BP and interprets combined sediment indicators and rice remains as cultivation; Zheng supports cultivation using different rice specimens. Converted dates are correct and approximate.
Only the sampled sequence is dated. The contrasted oak/pine interpretation and unverified barrier are disclosed as unresolved.

unknowns: The inferred wetland does not itself document an excavated field layout or transfer to later systems.

duplicate_screen.method: Compared base record events and searched all discoveries for Jiahu, Donghulin, Kuahuqiao, Shangshan, Shimoyakebe and Caoxieshan.
duplicate_screen.result: Donghulin grain event extends existing millet record: different evidence from earlier starch events. Kuahuqiao cultivation is distinct from Shangshan morphology and later Lake Tai field designs. Existing Jiahu beverage and carp records cover different activities. No duplicate discovery found.

unknowns: Kuahuqiao pig feeding strategy and any crop-to-pig dependence are not established.
The Tianluoshan comparison is cited by author, title and locators in an unresolved note, but lacks a registered source; add it if promoted to a retained formal event or relation.

Unchanged baseline millet summary gives 11,000–9,500 years although the Nanzhuangtou site interval starts 11,500 calibrated BP; the source distinguishes site age from age assigned to millet use. This baseline wording was not silently reapproved.

history.subsequent_vocabulary_issue: Original builds_on candidate was misclassified: vocab requires development out of the other, whereas evidence raised a possible feeding arrangement. Coordinator notified and requested repair.

vocabulary_attestation.basis: companion_of means the two worked together as parts of one arrangement. The revised question specifies an integrated feed arrangement; it is not accepted as established. Candidate status denotes a research question. builds_on was unsuitable because development out of the other was not the predicate.
